hook.text: The US pays 70% of NATO's defense bill. Most European allies spend below the 2% GDP target. Americans are tired.

buildup.text: Burden sharing is NATO's oldest argument. Free-riding allies let the US carry the weight while spending on welfare.

discovery.text: Unequal burden sharing breeds resentment. US leaders from Obama to Trump demanded Europeans pay their fair share.

twist.text: After 2022, European defense spending surged. Germany committed an extra $100 billion. Fear works better than nagging.

climax.text: The burden-sharing debate reveals a deeper issue: can Europe defend itself without the US? Not yet.

punchline.text: Sharing the load matters when the load gets heavier.

quiz.question: What percentage of NATO's defense spending does the US roughly cover?
